title: p256-ecdlp: deterministic negation-map BSGS with a complete cold-work ledger

claims.statement: For uniform x in [0,r), input Q=[x]P for the fixed SEC 2 Section 2.4.2 P-256 generator P (curve y^2=x^3-3x+b), recover x. The deterministic baby-step/giant-step algorithm in proof.md keys its table by affine x-coordinate (negation map), uses m=2^127 records, stride 2m-1 and h=2^127+1 giant iterations, covers exactly 2^255+2^127-1 scalars and therefore succeeds with probability strictly above 1/2 (hence at least 0.39), using less than 2^145 total target-group-operation equivalents, including preprocessing, routed memory access, sorting, failure paths and verification. No reference operation is used (H=0): every P-256 field operation (4-limb CIOS Montgomery multiplication, Fermat inversion), every complete affine point step (with the a=-3 doubling formula and its own inversion), all memory routing and control are charged through explicit analytic scalar AArch64 instruction bounds, and the total instruction count is divided by the borrowed normalization C=1000. Preprocessing is less than 2^145 equivalents and is included in total work; peak memory is less than 2^150 bytes; nonuniform advice is 0 bytes. There is no heuristic, randomness, retry or quantum step. This is an analytic conservative accounting control, not a claim of novelty or practical execution.

experiments.purpose: Exhaustively check the signed-window negation-map BSGS coverage and sign logic on small additive groups and on small prime-order curves y^2=x^3-3x+b and generic y^2=x^3+ax+b with real x-coordinate keys and complete affine addition; execute the counted 4x64-bit CIOS Montgomery multiplication and the Fermat inversion chain on the real P-256 prime; check the exact integer success and ledger inequalities with the real P-256 order. Finite scope only; does not establish production cost or security.
